 San Mateo County Property Owners Face Deadline To Appeal Tax Assessments
 A new online portal allows homeowners to challenge assessed property values without visiting county offices.
 Sanestina Hunter , Patch Staff 
 Posted Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 10:31 pm PT BURLINGAME, CA — Burlingame and Hillsborough property owners have until Nov. 30 to appeal their assessments through a new online system.
 For the first time, residents can submit formal appeals entirely online, eliminating the need to mail paperwork or visit county offices in Redwood City, according to a county news release published Friday. 
 The new portal allows property owners to review appeal requirements, gather information and submit applications electronically.

 Subscribe By subscribing, you agree to Patch's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use . County officials encourage residents to use the online system, saying it can reduce common filing errors and processing delays.
 “Processes that took sometimes months can be done now in a fraction of the time,” Assessment Appeals Board Clerk Maria Moon said in the release.
 Find out what's happening in Burlingame-Hillsborough for free with the latest updates from Patch. 
 Subscribe By subscribing, you agree to Patch's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use . “It has cut our manual work significantly, allowing me to respond more quickly and efficiently to the community we serve,” Moon added.
 The portal also provides a centralized location for property owners and professionals who handle multiple assessment appeals.
 David Alberti, a Redwood City property owner, used the system in September and described the process as straightforward. He later recommended it to another resident seeking information about filing an appeal.
 Real estate professionals have also reported improvements in accessibility and convenience, according to the county.
 The appeals process gives property owners an opportunity to formally challenge their property's assessed value.
 Residents interested in filing can review instructions and submit applications through the county's Assessment Appeals Board website .
